com.esignal.jstandard.managers

Interface TriggeredQuoteEventManager

  • All Superinterfaces:
    QuoteManager, ResourceManager

    public interface TriggeredQuoteEventManager
extends QuoteManager
    Purpose of this class is to provide resources of Triggered Quotes. TriggeredQuoteEventManager extends the functionality of the QuoteManager. Please refer to the documentation for QuoteManager here. TriggeredQuoteEventManager will allows users to do everything that can be done in the QuoteManager and provides capabilities that push the latest image of a selection of instruments to a subscribed client via a persistent connection when the following event occurs:
    • Field Trigger: When a particular field (e.g. settlement) is published, the system disseminates the image of the security at the time of that field. Currently understood to be limited to a single field being updated.

    The expected workflow for the snap on trigger requirement is as follows:

    • Client application establishes a persistent connection to ICE's API Servers
    • Client application sends a list of subscriptions, the fields which are expected to trigger an update, and an optional parameter of the fields expected to be returned (A trigger set).
    • On the field being updated: ICE will send a data object containing the image of a security/instrument containing default field set, or the field set specified
    • As an example, if Settlement was selected as the field, we would trigger an update every time settlement was published (even if that was multiple times in a day)

    Triggers can be added for fields and symbols using the call to addTrigger(String, TriggeredQuoteEventListener) .

    Removing an added trigger can be done by using the call to removeTrigger(String, TriggeredQuoteEventListener) .
    Note that the triggerName is the same unique (case sensitive) triggerName that was used when adding a trigger.

    The users are required to pass in a TriggeredQuoteEventListener for each trigger that they add or remove using addTrigger() and removeTrigger() calls.
    TriggeredQuoteEventListener has onTriggerAdded, onTriggerRemoved, onTriggerAcknowledged and onError methods that need to be implemented by the client.

    • onTriggerAdded is called asynchronously when you call addTrigger method call.
    • onTriggerRemoved is called asynchronously when you call removeTrigger method call.
    • onTriggerAcknowledged is called asynchronously when addTrigger and removeTrigger method calls are acknowledged on the server.
    • onError will be called for any issue with the addTrigger and removeTrigger calls, including the error code.

    All the Quote updates are sent to the TriggeredQuoteEventListener for those fields and symbols defined in the addTrigger JSON request string.
    Multiple listeners can be attached for the same symbol by calling addTrigger method by passing in a unique (case sensitive) triggerName but with the same triggerId multiple times with different TriggeredQuoteEventListener. After a successful addTrigger, the listeners will start listening to the streaming quotes, the updated Quote information can be retrieved using the TriggeredQuoteEvent fired with new data. We will run through a simple usage of TriggeredQuoteEventManager.

    Let's create a factory first. The ResourceManagerFactory.getFactory() method will retrieves the default implementation of the Factory. The implementation can be changed by calling other getFactory(...) methods OR overriding property "jstandard.resourcemanagerfactory.name" in jstandard.properties. ResourceManagerFactory factory = ResourceManagerFactory.getFactory();

    Now create a TriggeredQuoteEventManager using the factory. TriggeredQuoteEventManager triggeredQuoteEventManager = factory.createTriggeredQuoteEventManager();

    To start the connection we now need to create instances of ConnectionSettings and ConnectionListener.
    (Implement MyConnectionListener) 

            
        ConnectionSettings myConnectionSettings = new ConnectionSettings("myhost", "myusername", "mypassword");
        //If proxy settings are required 
        //myConnectionSettings.setProxyInfo("phost", pport, "puser", "ppass");
        ConnectionListener myConnectionListener = new MyConnectionListener();
        triggeredQuoteEventManager.connect(myConnectionSettings, myConnectionListener);
    At the start the connection listener will receive an event of connecting and after successful connection connected event.

    To start receiving updates for the symbol, let's addTrigger to the TriggeredQuoteEventManager with "AAPL" symbol. But before that we also need to have an implementation of the TriggeredQuoteEventListener. Let's say we have two listeners: LoggerTriggeredQuoteEventListener and MyTriggeredQuoteEventListener. 

     
 TriggeredQuoteEventListener loggerTriggeredQuoteEventListener = new LoggerTriggeredQuoteEventListener();
 TriggeredQuoteEventListener myTriggeredQuoteEventListener = new MyTriggeredQuoteEventListener();
 triggeredQuoteEventManager.addTrigger("{ "triggerName" : "trigger1", "triggerID" : 1234, "triggerType" : "field", "symbols" : [ "AAPL" ], "fields" : [ 21 ] }", loggerTriggeredQuoteEventListener);
 triggeredQuoteEventManager.addTrigger("{ "triggerName" : "trigger2", "triggerID" : 1234, "triggerType" : "field", "symbols" : [ "AAPL" ], "fields" : [ 21 ] }", myTriggeredQuoteEventListener);
    Now both the listeners will start receiving the updates on the same quote AAPL.

    To receive the updated data please implement TriggeredQuoteEventListener's onUpdate method. From QuoteEvent get the Quote object which could have one or more updated fields. There are two ways to read the field's values:

    • Call Iterator.next() after calling Quote.iterator() (preferred). Always call Iterator.hasNext() prior to calling Iterator.next().
    • Call Quote.getFieldItem(short) for each fieldId you are interested in. Always call Quote.isFieldItemNull(short) prior to calling Quote.getFieldItem(short).
    Both methods return a Quote.FieldItem. A Quote.FieldItem is composed of an Id, format and value. The JStandard Field Mappings page of https://developer.theice.com contains mappings of Field Id to LRT. These values are also defined as constants in Quote.FieldItem and are included in the Quote.FieldItem javadoc. Example, Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_BID is integer 20. Use these constants in your code to make your code more readable. New codes may be added in the future. The Quote.FieldItem methods allow the API user to access one or more field values using FieldItem.getValue* methods. Each field is uniquely identified by it's ID and format which should be cross referenced with meta data on the customer portal. See following examples: fieldId=1 means LRT_TYPE_CATEGORY and has value in the format of FIELDFORMAT.BYTE, thus calling Quote.FieldItem.getValueAsChar() will return 'char' value. fieldId=13 means LRT_TYPE_SYMBOL and has value in the format of FIELDFORMAT.STRING, thus calling Quote.FieldItem.getValueAsString() will return 'String' value. fieldId=50 means LRT_TYPE_52WEEKHIGH and has value in the format of FIELDFORMAT.DOUBLE, thus calling Quote.FieldItem.getValueAsDouble() will return 'double' value. Note that the Quote.iterator() is implicit in the for loop below. 
     
public void onUpdate(QuoteEvent event) {
        try {
                final Quote quote = event.getQuote();
                for (Quote.FieldItem item : quote) {
                        switch (item.getId()) {
                        case Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_CATEGORY: // 1
                                final char categoryCode = item.getValueAsChar();
                                System.out.println("CATEGORY CODE value:" + categoryCode);
                                break;
                        case Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_SYMBOL: // 13
                                final String symbol = item.getValueAsString();
                                System.out.println("SYMBOL value:" + symbol);
                                break;
                        case Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_52WEEKHIGH: // 50
                                final double high52Week = item.getValueAsDouble();
                                System.out.println("HIGH52WEEK value:" + high52Week);
                                break;
                        default:
                                System.out.println("Default value:" + item.getValue());
                        }
                }
        } catch (Exception e) {
                e.printStackTrace();
        }
}

    Let's say we decide to call removeTrigger(String, TriggeredQuoteEventListener) from the LoggerTriggeredQuoteEventListener for the symbol AAPL. Use the same instance that was created when we added the trigger. Remember removeTrigger(String, TriggeredQuoteEventListener) is driven by the unique (case sensitive) triggerName. 

     
 triggeredQuoteEventManager.removeTrigger("trigger1", loggerTriggeredQuoteEventListener);
    Now only myTriggeredQuoteEventListener will receive updates for the quote AAPL.

    listAllTriggers(String) can be called synchronously to get a JSON response string of all the triggers added

    Disconnect from the manager in the end. 

     
 triggeredQuoteEventManager.disconnect();

    Since we did not removeTrigger for myTriggeredQuoteEventListener, calling disconnect will make sure appropriate calls are made before closing the connection.

    • Method Detail

      • addTrigger

        void addTrigger(java.lang.String jsonMessage,
                TriggeredQuoteEventListener triggeredQuoteEventListener)
        Triggers can be added for fields and symbols using the call to addTrigger(String, TriggeredQuoteEventListener).
        The addTrigger JSON request string has the following fields :
         
        {
                "triggerName" : "A unique (case sensitive) trigger name",
                "triggerID": any random integer id,
                "triggerType" : "field",
                "symbols" : [ "SymbolA", ..., "SymbolN" ],
                "fields" : [ 19, 20, ..., 21 ]
        }

        Note: The API is parsing the request and checks for invalid fields on the JSON request string.
        The API could return the below errors for invalid addTrigger method call:

        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_NAME_NOT_SPECIFIED : If the trigger name is not specified.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS : If the trigger name already exists.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_TYPE_NOT_SPECIFIED : If the trigger type is not specified.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_SYMBOLS_NOT_SPECIFIED : If No symbol is specified.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_FIELDS_NOT_SPECIFIED : If no LRT field is specified.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_JSON_INVALID : for malformed JSON in the JSON request string.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_NOT_SPECIFIED = trigger def not specified.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND = trigger with that name not found.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_CONNECTION_CLOSED = connection closed.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_JSON_INVALID = If the trigger JSON is invalid.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_INVALID_SYMBOL_SPECIFIED = If the trigger symbol specified is invalid.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_INVALID_FIELD_SPECIFIED = If the trigger field specified is invalid.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_INVALID_TYPE_SPECIFIED = If the trigger type specified is invalid.
        Parameters:
        jsonMessage - is a JSON request string containing all necessary parameters needed to add a trigger.
        triggeredQuoteEventListener - TriggeredQuoteEventListener for receiving asynchronous responses.

      • removeTrigger

        void removeTrigger(java.lang.String triggerName,
                   TriggeredQuoteEventListener triggeredQuoteEventListener)
        Removing an added trigger can be done by using the call to removeTrigger(String, TriggeredQuoteEventListener) .
        Note that the triggerName is the same unique (case sensitive) triggerName that was used when adding a trigger.

        The API could return the below errors for invalid removeTrigger method call:

        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_NAME_NOT_SPECIFIED : If the trigger name is not specified.
        • DBCAPI_TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND : If the API cannot find the triggerName.

        Parameters:
        triggerName - The unique (case sensitive) trigger name used when calling addTrigger.
        triggeredQuoteEventListener - TriggeredQuoteEventListener for receiving asynchronous responses

      • listAllTriggers

        java.lang.String listAllTriggers(java.lang.String requestJson)

        listAllTriggers(String) can be called synchronously to get a JSON response string of all the triggers added
        With '"detailed": false' or not existent in a string representation of JSON request, you will get a string representation of JSON as follows:
        Request : 

        
        {
            "version": "1.0",
            "request": {
                "requestType": "listTriggers"
            }
        }
        Response : 
        
        {
            "version": "1.0",
            "responseType": "listTriggers",
            "payloadVersion": "1.0",
            "payload": [
                "trigger1",
                "trigger2"
            ]
        }
        With '"detailed": true' in a string representation of JSON request, you will get a string representation of JSON response as follows:
        Request: 
         
        {
            "version": "1.0",
            "request": {
                "requestType": "listTriggers",
                "params": {
                    "detailed": true
                }
            }
        }
        Response: 
         
        {
            "version": "1.0",
            "responseType": "listTriggers",
            "payloadVersion": "1.0",
            "payload": [
                {
                    "triggerName": "trigger1",
                    "triggerType": "field",
                    "symbols": [
                        "IBM",
                        "ES #F"
                    ],
                    "fields": [
                        19,
                        20,
                        21,
                        273
                    ]
                },
                {
                    "triggerName": "trigger2",
                    "triggerType": "field",
                    "symbols": [
                        "IBM"
                    ],
                    "fields": [
                        19,
                        20,
                        21
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
        Response is null if there are no triggers added or if there is an error processing the request.

        Parameters:
        requestJson - a string representation of JSON request to get all the triggers added
        Returns:
        a string representation of JSON with the list of added triggers. Null if there are no triggers added or if there is an error processing the request.
